newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Finnish cargo forwarder sees 15 pct growth '96.
newsitem.headline: Finnish cargo forwarder sees 15 pct growth '96.

text.p: Finnish freight forwarder Nystrom & Co said on Wednesday air cargo exports from Finland would rise by 15 percent in 1996 despite a lull during the summer.

"So far it looks like we could increase it by 15 percent or so. The summer was quite quiet this year but we think we can still manage it," the company's air freight sales manager Hans Gustavsson told Reuters by telephone from Helsinki.
The forecast was in line with the company's air freight shipments over the past few years.
"Globally, we have seen 15 to 16 percent growth per year starting in, let's say, 1990," Gustavsson said.
Nystrom & Co Oy AB, a medium-sized surface and air freight forwarder based at Helsinki's international airport, exported about 1,100 tonnes in 1995. Imports last year totalled around 700 tonnes.
"I see imports increasing but not like the exports. Companies are cautious in their thinking right now, wondering if they should import or not," Gustavsson said.
He estimated that imports would grow by 10 percent but said that it probably would not be more than that.
"There could be growth of 10 percent, but it could be tough," he said.
Gustavsson said U.S. destinations such as Chicago, Atlanta and Dallas were important for the company, as well as London and Manchester in the UK.
Nystrom & Co also exports goods, mainly Finnish-made electronics, to the Far East and South America.
